answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments function as a cryptographic inlet for identity integrity, forcing agents to map unique secret keys to global state transitions through verifiable delay functions that induce a temporal spiral of exponential difficulty. By coupling these commitments with VRF-based sortition and proportional slashing penalties, the protocol reaches a summit of security where the negative expected utility of cloning attacks renders identity forgery computationally infeasible under BFT consensus.
